items.prompt: Black to move. Win material by forcing the guard of f1 away.

claims.statement: ...Be3+ wins material along the engine line.
Only the king on g1 guards the queen on f1.

hints: Which white piece guards the queen on f1?
Can you give a check that makes that piece leave g1?
Check the king from e3.
items.explain: The check on e3 forces the king to h1, which leaves the queen on f1 without a guard. Qxf1 is then mate.

items.prompt: Black to move. The white king stands on b1. Does ...Rxa2 still win material? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The king and the queen both defend the rook on a2.
The engine rates the position as level.

hints: Count the defenders of the rook on a2.
Who can recapture on a2 other than the queen?
Kxa2 leaves the queen free to guard the bishop.
items.explain: A second piece now defends the rook, so the queen is no longer forced to recapture and keeps guarding the bishop. The queen is not overloaded any more.

items.prompt: Black to move. Is there a tactic that wins material?

claims.statement: The queen and the pawn on h4 both defend the bishop on g5.

hints: List every piece the white queen defends.
Does the queen have to leave the bishop to recapture?
Count the defenders of each target.
items.explain: The pawn on h4 guards the bishop, so the queen can recapture on a2 without giving up the bishop. The queen has only one job that needs it, so nothing is overloaded.

items.explain: The pawn on h2 also defends the rook on g3. Taking the knight on e2 removes only one of two defenders, so the idea wins nothing.

Look along the diagonal from d3.
Qxf1+ is met by which recapture?
items.explain: The bishop on d3 sees f1, so after the king leaves the queen is still guarded. Another piece took over the duty.

items.explain: The knight on g3 also guards f1, so forcing the king away does not leave the queen loose: ...Be3+ Kh1 Qxf1+ Nxf1 is only a queen trade. The deflection wins nothing.
